_comment: 8b R1 (issue #10). ~24x16 timber-and-thatch village (art direction: 'harvest light'). biome riverfarm_village = floodplains floor family on purpose (open-countryside continuity); village identity comes from PROPS + the wheat/loam floor_layers bands below, not a new floor tile. Reachable ONLY via the portal contract (data/portals.json's new 'riverfarm' row, requires_accomplishment riverfarm_attuned, banked by the Guild-board rumor beat) -- no door chain from the inn (per wi-adding-a-scene's reachability rule, an anchor-stone region is its own explicit exception, same as the ruin's door_when gate before it, just one layer further: portal-gated rather than door_when-gated). The witch_hollow path (riverfarm_hollow_path) is the map's own second exit, a treeline gap not a literal door.
_comment_cover_skip: Playtest hotfix #7b/7a: every blocked cell on this map is footprint for a building/fence/earthwork or the river -- none of them is bare dirt. The generic blocked-cell overlay tile (Wall_Tiles[14,4], a brown dirt/plank crop) painted a brown patch under every one of them, fighting the grass under buildings and hiding the river's own blue water tile entirely (world.gd's _build_floor paints floor_layers THEN the blocked overlay on top, per cell, unless listed in cover_skip -- the #37 mechanism). cover_skip == blocked verbatim: every cell here is already fully dressed by a real sprite or a real floor_layers tile, so skipping the generic overlay lets that real art show through instead.

Tilled loam plot (wang tile 0, pure loam) -- crop_row decor sits on top.

The river -- Free Pack Water_tiles.png (picks.md sec.2 col2/row7 was PIXEL-FLAT, 1 unique color across the whole 16x16 region, PIL-verified; VISUAL-LOG's issue #30 ART/WATER fix already proved col1/row5 genuinely textured, 5 distinct blue shades, near-identical hue -- reused verbatim here instead of introducing a third variant), same floor_layers mechanism as the wheat band above (handoff open-question 2: static bank row, no animation seam this task; the shimmer OVERLAY -- world.gd's water_shimmer, keyed to walls-segment water only -- is a separate, still-open mechanism decision, not this pick).

entities._comment: The north-edge earthworks -- the emperor's rising works hinted as DRESSING ONLY (Laken himself out of v1 scope, spec sec.1/handoff canon flags). Non-interactive; blocks its own 7x2 footprint.
entities.observe: Fresh-turned earth, packed and raised into a long low wall. Someone's been digging with purpose, not just drainage.
entities.toast: Just raised earth. Whatever it's for, nobody's finished it yet.

entities._comment: The longhouse is a REAL door now, not a toast prop -- same entity, same footprint cell, sprite/tint/visual_states untouched (the BRIGHTEN entry below still fires on blight_lifted whether the entity is read as prop or door; visual refresh is kind-agnostic). CONSTRAINT: cell (11,7) is the footprint's own south-face row (the blocked rampart at rows 6-7 spans cols 8-14; the sprite's anchor puts its visible door at x-center ~11, y near the bottom of the frame) -- approached from the open cell one row further south (11,8), facing up. to_cell (5,5) lands one row inside `riverfarm_longhouse`'s own south gap, facing away from the exit, matching the guild_door/guild_exit offset convention.
entities.observe: One long thatch ridge, twice the width of any cottage. Smoke curls from a vent at the peak even in daylight.
Clay-daub walls, a low thatch roof. A washing line strung between two posts.
entities.toast: Someone's home. Best not to just walk in.

entities.observe: A second cottage, smaller, its thatch newer than its neighbor's.
entities.toast: Someone's home. Best not to just walk in.

entities._comment: The tall silhouette that reads 'farming village' from anywhere on the map (art direction card, landmark read 1). Anchor.y is the base masonry, not frame bottom -- sails overhang above the blocked footprint.
entities.observe: Sails turning slow in whatever wind there is. The grinding floor above the wheat fields.
entities.toast: The sails creak overhead. No one's tending it right now.

entities.observe: A stone-ringed well, rope worn smooth by years of hauling. The water's clean this far from the blight talk.
entities.toast: Cool water, a long way down. You leave the rope where you found it.

entities.observe: Bundled and stacked before the rain, the way a good harvest gets stored.
Straw and an old coat, arms out over the tilled rows. It isn't working today -- there are crows on its own hat.
A plank pier reaching out over the river. The village's whole trade with anywhere downstream starts here (wiki Riverfarm, ch. 3.00-3.01 E: 'farming land fed by a river').
entities.toast: Weathered planks, sound underfoot. The current runs steady past the end of it.

entities._comment: The headman -- quest-giver. R3 (issue #11) wires the real conversation graph (riverfarm_headman.json): gives price_of_a_favor, closes it on any path's blight_lifted. Voice per profiles-staging: suspicious-then-warmer, farm metaphors, swallows apologies halfway. Issue #62 finding 15: facing flipped up->down -- every canonical approaches him from the SOUTH (village_edge/(11,10), 'Teleport doesn't carry facing -- re-face up' toward him in riverfarm_fight/riverfarm_talk/riverfarm_skill), so `up` had him showing his back to the player he's talking to; `down` faces the approach. #63 canon pass: display_name/speaker renamed The Headman -> Former Headman (wiki-verified: Riverfarm answers to Emperor Laken Godart's Unseen Empire now; the placing line lives in riverfarm_headman.json's authority_topic node).
talk_pool: We don't truck with witches here. Didn't used to, anyway.
A bad crop year, you learn to count what's yours twice. Once for the harvest, once for what walked off with it.
Sorry, I don't mean to- never mind. Long nights lately.
Wolves didn't used to come this close to the fences. Whatever's stirring up that hollow is pushing everything our way, wolves included.
entities.observe: A ledger under one arm, mud to the knee, the look of a man doing three jobs badly instead of one job well.

dialogue.speaker: Former Headman
dialogue.text: Not now. Got a village to hold together.

entities._comment: The charmed villager -- the quest's pivot. talk_pool carries the ONE echo_of entry (locked shape 3): WISocial resolves it to riverfarm_witch's CURRENT pool line verbatim at pick time. R3 (issue #11) retires the tell via talk_pool_stages (the existing pool-stage machinery, social.gd's last-met-wins walk): once blight_lifted lands, the freed-villager stage's OWN plain-string lines fully replace the echo_of entry -- no more echo, ever, any path.

lines: Thank you. I don't think I said that right the first ten times I tried.
I keep counting days like the price is still running. Old habit. I'll lose it eventually.
Ask me again sometime, once I've had more practice sounding like myself.

entities.observe: Ordinary, except for how still they stand, and a faint red thread at the wrist that doesn't match anything else they're wearing.

entities._comment: The village's fourth NPC (issue #10/#11 FIX-FIRST): a local [Hunter] (canon-attested profession, wiki.wanderinginn.com/Riverfarm) who carries the come-along beat -- data/dialogue/riverfarm_hunter.json's `hub`->`agreed` ask banks `hunter_will_come`, which is the ONLY thing that fields `riverfarm_hunter` as an ally on river_wolf_pack/briar_collectors/briar_collectors_deep (their ally_requires). Placed at (13,10), open ground between the well (11,11) and the headman (11,9) -- clear of every blocked cell and every other entity's cell, no trigger_radius so no blast-radius overlap with anything nearby.
talk_pool: Hollow's quieter than it should be. Doesn't sit right.
Lost two lambs to something with thorns for teeth. Wasn't a wolf.
Know that treeline better than the headman does. He'd rather not.
Wolf sign's getting thicker toward the hollow, week by week. I'm not walking that treeline for my health.
entities.observe: Weathered hands, a hunting knife worn plain at the hip, eyes on the treeline more than on you.

entities._comment: Riverfarm's OWN end of the anchor-stone-per-region idiom (portals.json's new 'riverfarm' row). Playtest hotfix #6: sprite swapped `boulder` -> `anchor_waystone` (a bespoke waystone-archway silhouette, not a rock), same tint precedent as street_anchor_stone. Gated on door_awakened (the SAME base network every anchor shares) -- reaching this cell at all already implies riverfarm_attuned (the ONLY way here is via another anchor's menu, itself door_awakened-gated), so the `light` below is unconditional (no visual_states gate needed) -- a stronger, steady glow every time this cell is ever seen.
entities.observe: A worn marker stone at the village's heart. Someone scratched a spiral into its face, long since softened by weather.
entities.toast: Cold, plain stone. Whatever it was for, it isn't for anything now.

entities.observe: A narrow break in the treeline, west of the fields. The light changes past the first few trees.

entities._comment: LOCKED interface (8b plan): encounter id river_wolf_pack, arena village_edge_night, on_victory survived_wolf_night (lane beta/R2). encounter_when is the phase-conditional spawn gate (spec sec.5) -- checked at interact() and _check_trigger_radius(), same sites door_when-class gates already run. trigger_radius 1 gives the NIGHT ambush read R2's harness rationale calls for; at day the gate refuses BEFORE start_combat runs (canonical-pinned NEGATIVE, riverfarm_walkthrough). entities.observe: Eyes catch the light at the field's edge, gone again when you look straight at them. Only after dark.
entities.gate_closed_toast: Nothing there. Whatever you saw is gone with the light.
